summary: Integrate Martech SDK into AI Design (iOS)
description:
Put MartechKit into AI Design (iOS). Phase 1 of the pilot — integration only. Proving the integration is correct is a separate story (Verify AI Design (iOS)).

Blocked by MTSDK-10. The spike decides HOW an integration is verified, and that decision changes what a verifiable integration looks like. If the answer is SDK-boundary assertion rather than vendor API read-back, this app needs a debug flavour, a test transport seam and an injectable graph — retrofitting that after integrating is rework. Integrate once the spike has told us what 'integrated correctly' means.

Runs IN PARALLEL with the harness stories (MTSDK-48/49/50), not before or after them. The two inform each other: the harnesses need a real app to assert against, and the integration needs the harnesses to know whether it worked. Expect to iterate across both.

Note on MTSDK-9 / MTSDK-12 (misuse prevention): those spikes will remove 3rd-party SDK init methods from the public interface. They do NOT block this integration. The failure mode they guard against is a host app calling AppsFlyer/Amplitude/RevenueCat init directly — a clean integration that goes through Martech.configure() is forward-compatible with whatever they decide.

Acceptance criteria:
- AI Design (iOS) depends on MartechKit and calls Martech.configure() + requestATT
- No 3rd-party SDK (AppsFlyer, Amplitude, RevenueCat, Meta, TikTok, Firebase) is initialised directly by the app
- The app is wired to whatever verification seam the MTSDK-10 spike chose
- A debug build can be driven through the MTSDK-10 journey: configure, consent, fire view_screen_splash, make a purchase
- Every friction point, missing doc and surprising API is written down as it happens — raw material for the playbook (MTSDK-54)
- Time-to-integrate is recorded. It is the baseline for the whole portfolio rollout business case.

summary: Integrate Martech SDK into AI Design (Android)
description:
Put MartechPack into AI Design (Android). Phase 1 of the Android pilot — integration only. Verification is a separate story.

Blocked by MTSDK-10 (same reason as iOS: the spike defines what a verifiable integration looks like) and by MTSDK-25 (Platform Convergence). Integrating against the pre-parity Android API means integrating against a surface that is actively being reshaped — 17 stories are changing the key provider, the module hooks, the DI graph and the public accessors. Doing this before parity lands buys a rewrite.

The iOS integration (MTSDK-52) runs first regardless: MartechKit is the mature side, and everything iOS learns makes this one cheaper.

Acceptance criteria:
- AI Design (Android) depends on MartechPack and configures it through the post-convergence API
- No 3rd-party SDK is initialised directly by the app
- A debug build can be driven through the same journey as iOS
- Any place where the Android integration path differs from the iOS one is filed against MTSDK-25 as a parity defect — do not absorb the difference silently in the app
- Time-to-integrate is recorded and compared against iOS. A large gap is a parity failure, not an Android tax.

summary: Integration playbook: how to integrate and how to prove it works
description:
Write the document an app team reads to integrate the Martech SDK without talking to us.

This is what turns the pilot into a rollout. Until it exists, every integration costs an SDK engineer, and priority #1 (integrate every app in the portfolio) does not scale.

Coding instructions alone are not enough and are not the hard part. The playbook must cover verification: how to run the suite, how to read a failure, what to do when the numbers look wrong.

Blocked by the AI Design (iOS) verification story — the playbook is written from what the pilot actually learned, not from what we imagine an integration looks like.

Acceptance criteria:
- Covers integration for iOS, Android and (once it exists) Flutter
- Covers how to run the verification suite locally and in CI
- Contains a troubleshooting section keyed on the suite's actual failure messages
- Includes the friction log from the AI Design pilot — every surprise, in the order an integrator will hit it
- Validated by having someone outside the SDK team follow it end to end on a third app, unaided
- Names the owner and the support channel
